title: Nutritional Diversity of Ecuadorian Foods Through Large-Scale Multivariate Statistical Analysis
content: Knowing precisely what populations eat requires knowing what the foods they consume are made of. This study characterizes the nutritional composition of 996 Ecuadorian foods and beverages from the Food Chemical Composition Table of the Universidad San Francisco de Quito (USFQ), reconstructed and verified, distributed across eleven food groups and described through nineteen nutritional variables. One-way ANOVA with effect size (η² and ω²), Pearson correlations, and two dimensionality-reduction techniques were combined: principal component analysis (PCA) and Ward's hierarchical clustering. The eleven groups differed significantly across all nineteen variables (p <  0.05), with effects ranging from small for vitamin A (η² = 0.029) to large for carbohydrates and energy (η² = 0.59). The strongest correlation linked total fat and monounsaturated fatty acids (r = 0.882), followed by energy and fat (r = 0.790), outlining a dominant lipid-energy axis. Across the 427 foods with complete information, the first five components explained 66.9% of the variance, revealing a nutrient-density gradient that opposes energy and minerals to vitamin C, plus an independent lipid gradient. Hierarchical clustering distinguished four nutritional profiles, ranging from low-energy-density plant foods to nearly pure oils and protein- and cholesterol-rich animal-source foods. These findings show that Ecuador's food supply is organized around recognizable compositional patterns, offering a quantitative basis for research in nutrition, food epidemiology, and public policy.
